prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Checkout UI Strings (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Key" · longest unbreakable word 206px · one-line width 206px
  col 2: header "English" · longest unbreakable word 62px · one-line width 196px
  col 3: header "中文" · longest unbreakable word 18px · one-line width 184px
  col 4: header "日本語" · longest unbreakable word 25px · one-line width 283px
  col 5: header "العربية" · longest unbreakable word 55px · one-line width 187px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Rendering convention: the screenshot always shows the WHOLE table. Anything beyond the dashed box is not clipped; it is the part a reader reaches by scrolling sideways, so judge both what fits in the box at first sight and the cost of scrolling to the rest.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 360px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"Map checkout interface keys to their English, Chinese, Japanese and Arabic translations for review and comparison.","reading":"Scan the key column to identify a string, then read across the row to compare its translations; horizontal scrolling makes it harder to maintain that connection.","groups":["English, 中文, 日本語 and العربية are parallel language columns; their widths should reflect their different text lengths and wrapping behavior.","Key identifies each row and anchors the translations."],"keep_intact":["Dotted key identifiers are easiest to recognize and compare when kept whole.","Individual English and Arabic words, numerals and punctuation should remain intact where space permits."],"may_wrap":["Translation phrases can wrap at natural language boundaries, including within Chinese and Japanese text.","Shorter translations can use row height already created by longer translations in the same row.","In a viewport-only design, long identifiers and some words must split."]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[227,132,115,150,125],"idea":"Keep keys intact and show the complete English column at first sight, with naturally wrapping translations reached by horizontal scrolling."},{"name":"B","widths":[227,217,205,304,208],"idea":"Keep every cell on one line for uninterrupted comparison, accepting substantial horizontal scrolling."},{"name":"C","widths":[94,70,54,71,70],"idea":"Show all five columns within 359px so every language is visible at once, accepting frequent splits and tall rows."}]}
